function: Blockage detection, outside the seven areas: a 3D CNN autoencoder infers a per-antenna, per-delay-bin blockage mask from PDPs (p. 8); the beamforming using it is not learned (p. 10).
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match the record. Excluded for function (first code that applies; it is a research article with a learned PHY component, so source_type, survey, no_learning and above_phy do not apply). The only learned component, a 3D CNN autoencoder, does blockage detection, p. 8: "to infer the presence and spatial distribution of blockages using the power delay profiles of the channel". It is evaluated only on blockage-mask maps, confusion matrices and BAIER (Figs. 4-7, pp. 11-13). The paper treats this objective as separate from channel estimation, p. 2: "the objective of [22] is channel estimation rather than blockage detection", and describes it as localizing shadowed antenna regions (p. 3), which is close to the excluded localization and sensing functions. The beamforming that uses the map is not learned: greedy SNR-based antenna selection, codebook beam realignment, and an l1-regularized MMSE convex design, p. 10: "we employ standard convex approximations". The spectral-efficiency results (Figs. 8-9, p. 14) compare these classical schemes and do not say which detector feeds them. So the learned method does not solve area 3, and area 5 does not fit because it designs no beams, waveforms or resources that serve sensing. Borderline: the CNN also outputs a reconstructed post-blockage PDP (Fig. 3 p. 11, p. 9), but that output is never evaluated, so I did not read the work as area 2. If the reviewer includes it, no criterion is met on my reading: a custom spherical-wave simulator (p. 10); no stated train/test split or test in unseen conditions; no earlier learned baseline (only the heuristic [53] and the Neyman-Pearson test [38], p. 12); no parameter count, FLOPs or runtime (only the layer table, p. 9); and no code or data released.
